Subject: Question on streaming / partial generation billing

Hi Vanessa,

Quick question as we finish the SOW review for our pilot: when a client is consuming streaming responses from Redwood (our chat UI streams tokens as they arrive), how are partial generations counted on the invoice if a client disconnects mid-response or reconnects and the model resumes? Specifically:

- If a user disconnects after receiving 30 tokens of a 200-token completion, do we get charged for all 200 tokens or just the 30 delivered?
- If the client reconnects and the app re-requests the same completion (either automatically or via retry), is the duplicated output billed again?
- Do retries performed by our backend (exponential backoff) result in duplicated token charges and are there best-practice patterns to avoid that?

We're also compiling these answers for procurement — if there are any standard line items on the rate card or example invoice snippets that show streaming math, that would help.

Thanks,
Alex Murray
Sr. Product Manager — WarpCloud
[WarpCloud]

Alex — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Karthik for the infra/billing specifics and Sean for the commercial implications (discounts / rate card). High level answers below, and Karthik will add the implementation details. I'm attaching our streaming billing FAQ and an example invoice excerpt.

Summary (short):
- Billing is per-token emitted by the model (both prompt + completion tokens). If a stream is interrupted, you are billed for whatever tokens were produced server-side and sent to the client.
- Retries that cause the model to generate additional tokens will be billed for the extra tokens; duplicates count as separate generated tokens.
- We provide guidance and SDK helpers to avoid double-generation in retry scenarios (idempotency keys + resume tokens).

Next steps: Karthik will confirm the exact semantics for partial buffer flush vs. committed token accounting and recommend SDK flags you should set. Sean — can you confirm whether we can offer a one-time credit for WarpCloud's pilot to help mitigate perceived risk?

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Question on streaming / partial generation billing

Alex — diving into the technical billing behavior: happy to share specifics so you can pass to procurement.

1) Charging on partial streams:
- Billing is calculated from the model's generated tokens. We bill tokens that the runtime materializes (i.e., passes through the output pipeline), not simply what the client acknowledges. Practically, if the model produced 200 tokens but the socket dropped after 30 reached the client, the invoice will include those 200 generated tokens.
- We do have a "flush policy" for long tails: tokens buffered but not materialized to the stream (e.g., internal batching windows) are not billed until they're emitted. In normal streaming cases tokens appear incrementally and are billed when emitted.

2) Retries and duplicates:
- A retry that causes the model to re-generate the same completion will be billed for the second generation. We treat each generation instance as billable work.
- To avoid duplicates, use our SDK resume token header (Redwood-Resume-Id) and idempotency keys on the request. If you set a resume id on reconnect, the runtime will try to continue the previous session's KV cache and avoid re-sampling repeated prefixes where possible. There are limits: resuming only works within the same model version and within a short time window (default 2 minutes).

3) Backend retries policy recommendations:
- At application level: prefer resuming streams over blind re-requesting. If you must retry, check the runtime response headers for a "generation-commit" flag before deciding to retry.
- At network level: use exponential backoff with jitter and detect whether the server signaled a partial commit.

4) Rate-card / invoicing examples:
- Streaming tokens are priced at the same per-token rate as non-streaming completions under your hosted plan; there is no separate "streaming per-minute" line item.
- Example: Prompt 120 tokens + Completion 200 tokens => billed 320 tokens. If the runtime generated 200 tokens and you saw 30 before disconnect, invoice shows 320 tokens.

If you'd like, we can produce a short invoice mock-up showing a few scenarios (clean disconnect, resumed stream, duplicated retry) for procurement.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the detailed context. Commercial side: we appreciate WarpCloud's close collaboration on the pilot. A few notes on pricing/credits: 

- Baseline hosted API pricing applies to streaming token counts as described by Karthik. For your pilot, I'm authorized to offer a one-time $5k invoice credit to offset any unexpected duplicate-generation charges during the onboarding window. This is a blunt instrument but often helps procurement signoff.
- If you expect heavy retry behavior or long-lived sessions with frequent disconnects, we can also talk about a short-term usage cap or a trial discount tier so you won't be surprised by a single spike.
- Regarding long-term packaging: if WarpCloud wants predictable economics, we can model a Dedicated commit (reserved capacity) which gives a lower effective per-token price and removes the duplicate-charge shock for high-volume streaming workloads. I can put together a few committed-capacity pricing scenarios if you want to evaluate them versus hosted per-token.
